original_value: AbstractMotivationAlthough modern high-throughput biomolecular technologies produce various types of data, biosequence data remain at the core of bioinformatic analyses. However, computational techniques for dealing with this data evolved dramatically.ResultsIn this bird’s-eye review, we overview the evolution of main algorithmic techniques for comparing and searching biological sequences. We highlight key algorithmic ideas emerged in response to several interconnected factors: shifts of biological analytical paradigm, advent of new sequencing technologies and a substantial increase in size of the available data. We discuss the expansion of alignment-free techniques coming to replace alignment-based algorithms in large-scale analyses. We further emphasize recently emerged and growing applications of sketching methods which support comparison of massive datasets, such as metagenomics samples. Finally, we focus on the transition to population genomics and outline associated algorithmic challenges.

result.paraphrase: AbstractMotivationAlthough modern high-throughput biomolecular technologies generate many kinds of data, biosequence data remain central to bioinformatic analyses. Yet the computational methods used to handle them have changed dramatically.ResultsIn this bird’s-eye review, we summarize the development of the principal algorithmic approaches for comparing and searching biological sequences. We emphasize the key ideas that emerged in response to several linked forces: changes in biological analytical paradigms, the arrival of new sequencing technologies, and the substantial growth of available data. We discuss the rise of alignment-free methods, which are increasingly replacing alignment-based algorithms in large-scale analyses. We also highlight the recently emerging and expanding use of sketching methods for comparing massive datasets such as metagenomics samples. Finally, we turn to the shift toward population genomics and outline the related algorithmic challenges.
